kypExtensions.summary: The pattern/trap/pivot/recall/rapidReview attack structure layered over the printed table — 6 patterns (bethanechol for postoperative retention; the methacholine challenge test; pilocarpine for Sjögren xerostomia + glaucoma; the donepezil trio as Alzheimer first line; pyridostigmine as the long-acting myasthenia mainstay with glycopyrrolate/hyoscyamine; the farmer's DUMBBELLS presentation), 5 traps (bethanechol vs carbachol; neostigmine vs physostigmine; pyridostigmine vs neostigmine; atropine vs pralidoxime; physostigmine-as-poisoning-antidote), 3 pivots.
kypExtensions.rationale: First Aid supplies the DRUG/ACTION/APPLICATIONS table and the poisoning block only; the attack structure is a KYP design.

kypExtensions.summary: The four-move reading protocol (FORK / TARGET / APPLY / ROUTE) and the turn-the-lock vs jam-the-shredder framing of the page — a direct agonist is a receptor key; an indirect agonist jams AChE, the synapse's shredder, so endogenous ACh accumulates — including the one-drug-one-organ anchoring of the direct lane and the receptor-layer routing of poisoning management.
kypExtensions.rationale: The source prints two table halves side by side but never teaches the fork as a decision path; the protocol, the shredder metaphor, and the organ anchoring are KYP's synthesis.
kypExtensions.location: core.keyIdea + blocks[5] the steps block + blocks[4] the compare block + the registry visual's lane headers

kypExtensions.summary: The four KYP mnemonics (TURN THE LOCK OR JAM THE SHREDDER / ONE DRUG, ONE ORGAN / CHARGED STAYS OUT, UNCHARGED CROSSES IN / MUSCARINIC GETS ATROPINE, NICOTINIC GETS PRALIDOXIME). The source's OWN mnemonics print in the table cells ('Bethany, call me to activate your bladder.'; 'Carbon copy of acetylcholine'; 'You cry, drool, and sweat on your pilow.'; '(Dona Riva forgot the gala)'; 'Neo = no blood-brain barrier penetration'; 'Pyridostigmine gets rid of myasthenia gravis'; 'Phreely (freely) crosses blood-brain barrier'; physostigmine 'phyxes' atropine overdose; DUMBBELSS) — carried ATTRIBUTED to First Aid in the note's memory callout and verbatim tables, and NOT counted among the four KYP codes.
kypExtensions.rationale: The four ALL-CAPS codes (class-fork, organ anchoring, BBB charge rule, antidote routing) are KYP's design; none duplicates a printed mnemonic.
kypExtensions.location: mnemonics + blocks[7] the mnemonic-provenance callout + the registry visual's band footers

kypExtensions.summary: The farmer organophosphate-poisoning miniCase (malathion exposure with the full DUMBBELSS picture, nicotinic weakness, and lethargy; management question) — the correct option is atropine PLUS pralidoxime given early; the distractors are atropine alone (leaves the nicotinic neuromuscular blockade unopposed), pralidoxime alone (the printed coadministration rule — transient worsening — plus poor BBB leaving the CNS layer uncovered), and physostigmine (the mirror-image trap: it antidotes ANTICHOLINERGIC toxicity and would deepen cholinergic excess). Includes the enzyme-aging rationale behind the printed 'if given early' (pralidoxime must dephosphorylate AChE before the organophosphate-enzyme bond ages into permanence).
kypExtensions.rationale: First Aid prints the poisoning block as findings and reversers but never integrates them into a management vignette; the stem, the four distractor mechanisms, and the aging rationale are KYP's design.

kypExtensions.summary: The glaucoma outflow mechanics behind pilocarpine's printed parentheticals — ciliary-muscle contraction opens the trabecular-meshwork outflow pathway (the open-angle application) and pupillary-sphincter contraction pulls the iris out of the angle (the closed-angle application).
kypExtensions.rationale: Book 239 prints only the drug facts ('Contracts ciliary muscle of eye (open-angle glaucoma), pupillary sphincter (closed-angle glaucoma)') without the aqueous-outflow mechanics; the gloss used in the ophthalmology crossLink is standard pharmacology knowledge, recorded here so it is never presented as though it printed on the page.

notes: FULL PAGE (no shared split in the PH16-PH20 batch): pdf 261 / book 239 is entirely the Cholinomimetic agents subsection — one printed DRUG/ACTION/APPLICATIONS table under two spanning shaded subheaders (Direct agonists: bethanechol, carbachol, methacholine, pilocarpine; Indirect agonists (anticholinesterases): donepezil/rivastigmine/galantamine, neostigmine, pyridostigmine, physostigmine) plus the separate Anticholinesterase poisoning block (organophosphate intro; muscarinic DUMBBELSS / nicotinic / CNS rows with their printed reversers) and the indd footer. Edrophonium and echothiophate do NOT print on this page and are never quoted or claimed (the batch spec's 'whatever prints on the page' rule). CENSUS METHOD: pdfimages reports ZERO raster images on pdf 261 — pure text + table art; the VLM was AVAILABLE this session (unlike the ph6-ph10 batch's 401 outage): the full-page 120-dpi pass confirmed the table structure, both spanning subheaders, the poisoning block's findings-vs-reversal split, all the in-cell mnemonics, and the absence of figures/photographs, and ONE documented 200-dpi adjudication pass on the pilocarpine row resolved the interleaved text layer — 'Potent stimulator of sweat, tears, and saliva' sits in the APPLICATIONS column (both VLM passes agree), the mnemonic prints 'pilow' (the source's own spelling, confirmed at 200 dpi against the text layer), and the ACTION cell breaks 'blood-brain' across a printed line (the pdftotext layer merges it to 'bloodbrain' — an extraction artifact, NOT a source typo; the note's human-facing verbatim table shows the printed 'blood-brain' hyphenation and documents the merge, while the evidence quotes follow the text layer exactly). INTERLEAVE QUIRK (documented, the m38 convention): the text layer prints the two spanning subheader labels ('Direct agonists' at page-261 line 55, 'Indirect agonists (anticholinesterases)' at line 57) BETWEEN the pilocarpine row and the donepezil row; the logical table per the VLM render places them as spanning shaded rows above each half — quoted in physical text-layer order as one entry with the position documented. Other verbatim quirks carried and documented: the source's own mnemonics print IN the table cells (all carried attributed to First Aid in the note's memory callout + verbatim tables); the ↑ and → glyphs print in the text layer (with \x8f control bytes that the verifier strips); 'SEC TION II' is the header's own text-layer spacing artifact; the donepezil trio's entire ACTION cell prints as just '↑ ACh.'.
